reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.sigmaBrownian -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: the sigma-algebra generated by the Brownian motion up to time t (the W-part of "the
filtration generated by W, N and F_0", sec. 2): sigma(W^j_s : s <= t, j < d) (for a scalar BM
sigma(W_s : s <= t)). Faithful Lean: the supremum over s <= t (and over coordinates j) of the
comap sigma-algebras of W^j_s, as a sub-sigma-algebra of the ambient one (each W_s measurable).
Harmless: s ranging over [0,t] or over all s <= t in a nonnegative time type; generating by
increments W_s - W_r (r <= s <= t) instead of values, since W_0 = 0 (a.s.; if W_0 = 0 only a.s.
the two differ by a null-set-level difference absorbed by augmentation). Not faithful: the
sigma-algebra of all times (no t-truncation) when used as a filtration, or of a single
coordinate when d > 1.

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.sigmaBrownian (MultidimFiltered.lean:32-34)

Reading (locked): I expected a time-t sigma-algebra sigma(W_s : s <= t) and flagged "sigma-algebra
of all times (no t-truncation) when used as a filtration" as not faithful.
Lean: sigmaBrownian W := sup_t comap (W.W t) (Borel) = sigma(W_t : t in R), the sigma-algebra of
the WHOLE process. Its role in the definition closure: LevyDriver.indep :
Indep (sup_i sigmaBrownian (W.W i)) (sigmaPoisson N) P, i.e. sigma(W) independent of sigma(N), the
paper's "W and an independent Poisson random measure N" (sec. 2). It is never used as a
filtration (the time-t sigma-algebras are Martingale.naturalFiltration /
MultidimBrownianMotion.naturalFiltration). For that role the whole-process sigma-algebra is
exactly the right notion (independence of processes). Negative times: W_t = 0 a.s. for t < 0, so
those generators are P-trivial (prob. 0 or 1 sets), which does not change any independence
statement (a pi-system argument: intersections with P-trivial sets factor). Multi-dim: the
driver takes sup over coordinates, giving the joint sigma(W).
So my anticipated failure mode does not occur; the definition is sigma(W) as the paper uses it.
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Choice: the generators are W_t for all real t, negative t included; since W_t = 0 almost surely
for t < 0, these add only sets of probability 0 or 1, which leave the independence statement
LevyDriver.indep (the only definitional use) equivalent to sigma(W_t : t >= 0) independent of
sigma(N). The definition is the whole-process sigma-algebra sigma(W), which is the notion the
paper's independence of W and N needs; it is not used as a filtration.
